notes: ~7 kDa = 21 x ~330. Arithmetic estimate pending confirmed sequence/mod pattern.

notes: ~14 kDa arithmetic. Note SEC-MALS measured 17.15 kDa on a specific siRNA (SRC-ZYDNEY-2024).

notes: One residue (~330 Da) out of ~7000 Da strand = ~4.7%. Below any UF size-separation threshold.

name: Latent heat of vaporisation of water (approx 40-60 C vacuum)
scale_system: physical constant — water at reduced pressure
notes: ~2400 kJ/kg near 40-60 C; 2257 kJ/kg at 100 C. Standard steam-table value.

name: Ligation conversion
scale_system: measured — immobilised RNA ligase, fully modified siRNA blocks, 5 mL packed column, 600 uM
notes: PER-LIGATION conversion, NOT a step mass yield and NOT the overall mass yield (see P-YLD-LIG, P-YIELD-OVERALL-PUB). Measured >92 percent single-feed and >94 percent split-feed on fully modified siRNA blocks in continuous flow, held >100 h (SRC-CN119265174) - and note that the '>100 h' there is a CATALYST LIFETIME, not a hold time. THREE CONVERSION NUMBERS NOW EXIST IN THE REGISTERS AND NO TWO ARE COMMENSURABLE, which is the correction made 2026-09-25 and is more important than any one of them. SRC-USPTO-10640812 defines conversion verbatim as 'product area/(template + product area) * 100' and tabulates it; its Example 13 Table 22 instead reports a species distribution whose own caption is verbatim 'The percentage of each segment, intermediate and product is expressed as fractional peak area relative to the tri-template hub peak area' - an internal-reference-normalised COMPOSITION, a different denominator from that patent's own conversion table and a third from this row's 92 percent. So the earlier blanket claim that that patent 'reports RELATIVE PEAK AREA ONLY' is struck as false, but the fix must not go the other way: 89.50 percent and 92 percent MUST NOT be pooled, quoted as a range, or read as corroborating one another. A further caveat travels with the 89.50 percent - its substrate is stated verbatim to have 'all linkages are phosphodiester linkages', so the best-converting concentration in the record is on a backbone we do not have, and the same patent's phosphorothioate/MOE gapmer figures are 11.8 percent or less. The often-quoted 82-96 percent range is a ligase screen on an UNMODIFIED shortmer whose phosphorothioate donors reacted only ~30 percent (SRC-NATCOMM-2024); >95 percent is an unreviewed vendor claim traceable only to a marketing blog (SRC-CODEXIS, SRC-CODEXIS-PR-2024, SRC-CODEXIS-PATENTS). Our kg-scale value is open. See Q-010.

name: Block full-length purity
scale_system: measured — 4-5 nt MOE/DNA gapmer blocks, 145.5-258 g, chromatography-free (NOT our 5'-phosphate 2'-OMe/2'-F/PS blocks; NOT a 5'-phosphorylated block at all)
notes: BAND (evidence): chromatography-free full-length purity of 4-5 nt modified blocks at hectogram scale, measured 93.6% (145.5 g), 94.8% (190 g) and 95.6% (258 g) (SRC-WO2020227618). CORRECTED 2026-09-25, and the correction is the point of the row: the previous point value of 92 was not a purity at all but a YIELD - the source reads verbatim 'deoxy-TTACC 5mer (145.5 g, 57.8 mmol, 92.4% yield, 93.6% purity)', so 93.6% is that compound's purity and 92.4% is how much of it was recovered. The previous range_low of 89 was the 89.1% purity of compound 7-3-10 at 6.00 g - a BENCH datum presented as part of a '145-258 g' band, a 25-40x scale misattribution. The purity values in that document span 68.2-99.3% across 42 distinct figures; what restricts the band is the SCALE and the absence of chromatography, not a selection among them. A WIDER, ARGUED band covers the same variable from first principles: a 1-3% per-cycle failure rate gives 0.97^4 = 88.5% to 0.99^4 = 96.1% for a 5-mer (SRC-US6087491). That is a different kind of claim from a measurement and is carried separately rather than merged into this one. CHEMISTRY CAVEAT: these are MOE/DNA gapmer blocks, not our 2'-OMe/2'-F/PS blocks, and 81% was measured for a 6-mer 2'-OMe PS (SRC-KELLY-OPRD-2025), so 95%-class blocks are not assured in our chemistry. No measurement exists anywhere for a 5'-PHOSPHORYLATED short 2'-OMe/2'-F/PS block, which is the number this parameter claims to be - see Q-057. The earlier note asserted these blocks carry a 5'-DMTr purity handle 'a 5'-phosphate block lacks'; that is wrong and is struck - chemical phosphorylation reagents are DMT-ON-purification compatible, the phosphate being unmasked after purification. See Q-011 and the filtration finding.

name: Step yield: ligation + workup
scale_system: ASSUMPTION — placeholder
notes: Flagged assumption for the balance: ligation + workup STEP mass yield. A balance that reads a >92% per-ligation conversion as a step yield overstates output several-fold. See Q-012.

notes: BAND (vendor-published): overall mass yields of 19-43% for kilogram-scale ligation-built siRNA (Inclisiran P-to-P 26%, Divalent P-to-P 19%, C-to-P 43%; SRC-HONGENE-BROCHURE-2025). name: Ligation reactor product concentration
scale_system: demonstrated ~1 mM titre of a ~14-15 kDa duplex at 1 L scale (SRC-ALMAC-2023); not our kg-scale duplex
notes: Flagged assumption, and re-scoped 2026-09-25 to AN UPPER BOUND rather than a titre. Anchored to the only demonstrated enzymatic-ligation concentration: ~1 mM in jacketed 1 L vessels (SRC-ALMAC-2023), which for a ~14-15 kDa duplex is ~14-16 g/L (arithmetic ours); 15 g/L used. WHAT THAT SENTENCE ACTUALLY SAYS is the concentration at which synthesis was ACHIEVED, and the paper reports no conversion, yield or purity anywhere - verified by counting: the whole text contains exactly ONE percent sign, in '100% v/v methanol'. So the real product titre is lower than 15 g/L by an unstated margin and this row is a CEILING on the titre, which matters because it is used_by=balance and a ceiling read as a titre oversizes nothing but undersizes the vessel. The vendor 'up to 100 g/L' is a substrate LOAD, not a product titre, and the previously carried '30 g/L titre' is NOT in SRC-CODEXIS (Q-034). The span 1.5-10 mM that brackets the segment charge is NOT a range and is registered separately (P-LIG-SEG-CONC, Q-064). See Q-016.

name: UF max achievable concentration
scale_system: ASSUMPTION - siRNA basis; charged membrane raised achievable concentration from 52 to >180 mg/mL (bench)

scale_system: ASSUMPTION — placeholder
notes: Flagged assumption; sets dryer water load. See Q-019.

notes: Flagged assumption. Diafiltration clearance is molecule-independent theory (EQ-DIAF): the vendor diavolume table reproduces the site's removal percentages exactly (SRC-PALL-TFF; 5 DV=99.3%, 7 DV=99.9%) and the same relation the protein/mAb literature uses (SRC-BPT-TFF) applies unchanged to a nucleic acid, documented at 4-6 diavolumes (SRC-HUSSON-CIRCRNA-2025). See Q-020.

name: Excipient : API mass ratio (spray dry)
scale_system: ASSUMPTION — placeholder (trehalose matrix)
notes: Flagged assumption (trehalose matrix). Reframed by F-024: the excipient is a DRYING and POWDER-PROPERTY aid, not a chemical stabiliser - approved siRNA products are stable at 160-200 mg/mL in near-pure water and four of seven carry no weighed excipient (SRC-SIRNA-LABELS). So the ratio is set by what the DRYER needs, not the molecule; no dried siRNA product has ever been approved, so no ratio transfers. See Q-021.

scale_system: ASSUMPTION - base case adds bulk excipient after evaporation
notes: 0 = all excipient added after evaporation (base case); 1 = full load present at the final DF. Risk R-005 requires salts exchanged OUT at final DF but not the excipient load IN. Setting this to 1 with the current concentration placeholders leaves evaporation with almost no duty. See Q-038, Q-021.

name: Minimum wetting rate - falling-film evaporator (water)
scale_system: water on vertical stainless steel; NOT a polyelectrolyte solution, so surface tension and contact angle dominate and the transfer to our matrix is plausible but unproven
notes: BAND: reported minimum wetting rate 0.10-0.22 kg/m/s for water on vertical steel (SRC-HUGHES-2024). Sets evaporator turndown (R-013, R-004): below it the film breaks into rivulets and dry patches foul, so a small batch must recirculate rather than run single-pass. Water, not our matrix; the transfer is plausible but unproven. See Q-018.

name: Specific heat of the process solution
scale_system: dilute aqueous stream approximated as water
notes: Dilute aqueous solution approximated as water (4.18 kJ/kg/K, the cited steam-table value); drives the evaporator sensible-heat term. Our concentrated polyelectrolyte matrix will differ slightly. See Q-045.

name: Specific heat of the drying gas
scale_system: air or nitrogen at drying temperatures (standard value)
notes: Standard specific heat of air/N2 near drying temperatures (~1.0 kJ/kg/K); drives the derived drying-gas mass and the heater duty. NO PRIMARY SOURCE IS REGISTERED for this constant, which is why it is flagged inference rather than fact - it is a standard textbook value, not our reasoning, and registering a primary gas-properties source is an open action. Air is ~1.005-1.01 and N2 ~1.04, so 'air or nitrogen' is not a single value. See Q-046.

scale_system: ASSUMPTION - placeholder (near-ambient feed)
notes: Temperature of the retentate entering the evaporator; sensible heat raises it to the vacuum boiling point. Placeholder pending the thermal operating point. See Q-045.

scale_system: ASSUMPTION - vacuum operating point chosen to protect the duplex
notes: BAND: vacuum boiling point held low (40-60 C) so the duplex is never heated near its Tm; 50 C is the representative point. Boiling-point elevation rises as solutes concentrate (EQ-EVAP, EQ-BPE). See Q-045.

name: Spray-dryer inlet gas temperature
scale_system: ASSUMPTION - placeholder
notes: Drying-gas inlet temperature. While the droplet is wet the particle sits near the wet-bulb temperature, far below the inlet gas (spray-drying finding), so a hot inlet does not heat the product to inlet temperature. Placeholder pending the drying design. See Q-046.

scale_system: ASSUMPTION - held below the duplex Tm
notes: Outlet gas temperature held below the duplex melting temperature (Tm 58-64 C, Q-030) and used as a conservative proxy for the product; the powder must also stay below its moisture-shifted Tg (Q-039). Placeholder. See Q-046.

name: Thermal loss fraction (evaporator and dryer)
scale_system: ASSUMPTION - placeholder (heat loss to surroundings)
notes: Fraction added ONCE to the evaporator and dryer PROCESS duties for heat loss to surroundings; 5% placeholder pending the thermal design. It is not applied to the gas enthalpy drop, which already contains wall losses. See Q-045.

name: Drying-gas ambient temperature before the inlet heater
scale_system: ASSUMPTION - placeholder (near-ambient intake air)
notes: Temperature of the drying gas BEFORE the inlet heater. This is what makes the heater duty computable: UT-DRYGAS is inlet air/N2 heating, so the utility load is the gas mass times cp times (inlet - ambient), not the enthalpy drop across the dryer. Placeholder pending the drying design. See Q-046.

name: Process solution density (evaporator feed basis)
scale_system: ASSUMPTION - dilute aqueous approximated as water; a 150 g/L polyelectrolyte retentate runs nearer 1.05-1.08 kg/L
notes: Density converting the evaporator feed VOLUME into the MASS the sensible-heat term needs. Until now this conversion was implicit - litres were used directly as kilograms - so an unregistered number was entering the balance where no provenance guard could see it. The approximation is weakest exactly where it is applied, at the concentrated retentate. Placeholder. See Q-045.

name: Health-based exposure limit (HBEL/PDE) for cleaning validation
scale_system: ASSUMPTION - requires toxicology/PDE data that does not exist publicly for this molecule
notes: Value deliberately BLANK: no PDE/HBEL can be derived without toxicology data, which does not exist in the public record for this molecule, so it is registered as a gap rather than invented. The DERIVATION METHOD (PDE then MACO / limit per swab or rinse) is documented on the microbial page (SRC-WHO-TRS1044). Needed for cleaning validation of the shared, hard-to-clean evaporator and dryer (R-008, R-015). See Q-047.

name: Number of blocks assembled per strand
scale_system: demonstrated disconnections — 2/strand at 1 L and at kg GMP; 3/strand only at 0.1 mM in 96-well plates. Point value is OURS.
notes: Number of blocks ligated per strand, the exponent in the purity floor (EQ-PURITY). BAND (evidence): 2-3 per strand is what has been DEMONSTRATED. 2 per strand has three independent supports - the arm Almac took to 1 L at 1 mM (Approach 1, 4 blockmers, 2 ligation sites), Hongene's kg-scale GMP four-fragment inclisiran (SRC-HONGENE-BROCHURE-2025), and the four-fragment patisiran assembly. 3 per strand is demonstrated once, at 0.1 mM in 96-well plates (Almac Approach 3, 'the 6 blockmer strategy') - a 10x lower concentration and a plate-vs-1 L crossing that must travel with it. The POINT VALUE 3 is this project's assumed disconnection and remains an assumption, not the demonstrated case. The register's direction - more blocks means a lower floor - was re-checked and HOLDS, but only because EQ-PURITY freezes f while varying k; f is itself a function of block length, and the model does not say so. See Q-058, Q-011, Q-057.

name: Ligation ATP concentration
scale_system: SI Table S1 of SRC-ALMAC-2023, titled 'Reaction conditions for RNAL screening' - 96-WELL PLATE SCREENING at 0.1 mM blockmer, which is 10x BELOW the 1 mM titre demonstrated in the 1 L vessel; the paper reports no ATP concentration for the 1 mM / 1 L run
notes: The ATP concentration used in the SCREENING conditions of the only demonstrated fully modified siRNA ligation route (SRC-ALMAC-2023, SI Table S1). SCALE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 2026-09-25: this row previously claimed the figure for 'bench to 1 L'. It is not. Table S1 is titled 'Reaction conditions for RNAL screening' and runs at 0.1 mM blockmer in 96-well plates - a tenth of the demonstrated titre - and the paper reports neither ATP nor enzyme loading for the 1 mM / 1 L run. That is this repository's signature defect, a bench number wearing a pilot label, and it was present in two rows at once (see P-LIG-ENZ-LOAD). Q-040 IS ALSO REWRITTEN, because the tension is real but far weaker than this note claimed. The 'at least 4 mM ATP' sentence in SRC-WO2025262452 is verbatim and appears twice, but it is the STATEMENT OF THE PROBLEM THAT DOCUMENT'S INVENTION SOLVES, not an operating condition: the same document teaches 'less than about 4 mM ATP ... optionally ... 0.5 mM or less' (four occurrences), says its ATP regeneration system 'overcomes the requirement for high concentrations of ATP', and claims complete ligation with 'sub-stoichiometric quantities of ATP or AMP'. The ceiling side is softer than stated too - SRC-PBCV1-2014 reports little inhibition at 1 mM ATP for most sequences. So there is NO window empty by 6-40x, and no such claim is written here; there is a coupling with a mechanism that reconciles it, registered in couplings.csv. The optimum still moves with the enzyme and its form (Q-050). See Q-040, R-010.

name: Ligation reaction temperature
scale_system: cited ligation temperatures span 16-30 C across two patents and neither is our kg-scale batch; SRC-CN119265174 runs BATCH at both 16 C (Examples 3, 7) and 25 C (Example 8) and its packed-bed flow example at 25 C, and SRC-USPTO-10640812's 25 C examples are where two chemistries FAILED
notes: Placeholder, and CORRECTED 2026-09-25 - the previous note's claim that 'both cited ligation examples run at 25 C' is wrong in both legs and the agreement it inferred does not exist. Re-read against the documents: SRC-CN119265174 runs batch ligations at 16 C for 16 h (Examples 3 and 7) AND at 25 C for 16 h (Example 8), so one document alone spans 16-25 C in the same regime. Worse, 25 C IS WHERE THINGS FAILED in SRC-USPTO-10640812: in Example 10 with Mg2+ 'no full length product was detected' and full length appeared only with Mn2+, and in Example 11 the Chlorella virus (SplintR) ligase gave verbatim 'At 25 C ... no full length product was observed. At 30 C. and 37 C., full length product was detected.' So 25 C is a point at which two of three exemplified chemistries produced no full-length product, not a demonstrated optimum. THE CEILING NAMES THE WRONG LIMIT TOO: this row and R-003 imply the duplex melting band (P-DS-TM 58.1-64.1 C) bounds it from above, but every retrieved ligation temperature is 30 C or below and the binding limit is ENZYME stability, far below the duplex's. The enzyme figure is NOT carried: the document behind it could not be retrieved, and the two numbers that circulated are midpoints of residual-activity curves after a 60 min hold rather than melting temperatures, so they must never be set against P-DS-TM as like-for-like (Q-059). No range is written here because the retrieved temperatures are a mix of successes and failures across three enzymes, which is not a band. See Q-050, Q-010, Q-030.

name: Ligation reaction hold time (batch)
scale_system: cited BATCH hold times only; the immobilised continuous-flow route is a different regime at 5-20 min residence (SRC-CN119265174) and is deliberately NOT folded into this band
notes: BAND (evidence): cited batch ligation hold times - 16 h (SRC-USPTO-10640812) and 24 h at 4 C one-pot (SRC-NAR-2025). Point value deliberately BLANK: the endpoints are different enzymes at different temperatures, so the band brackets what has been demonstrated and is NOT a predicted hold time for our reaction. CORRECTED 2026-09-25: this note previously said that SRC-USPTO-10640812 reports RELATIVE PEAK AREA ONLY and so does not close Q-010. That blanket negative is FALSE and is struck. The patent defines conversion verbatim ('Conversion = product area/(template + product area) * 100'), has a table column headed 'Conversion (%)', and Example 13 Table 22 is a nine-point time series whose values were re-read character-for-character. So the 16 h endpoint is now backed by a CURVE rather than by a single sample: 88.10 percent at 14 h rising to 89.50 percent at 16 h, i.e. the last two hours buy 1.40 points and the reaction is plateauing. BUT THE TWO TABLES ARE NOT COMMENSURABLE AND MUST NOT BE POOLED - see P-LIG-CONV. WHAT IS STILL WRONG WITH THE BAND, and it is disclosed rather than repaired: the 24 h high endpoint could not be verified against its document this session, so this is one measurement plus one unverifiable endpoint, not two independent measurements. Recorded as such in envelopes.csv (bracket_verdict measurement_plus_unverifiable). CHEMISTRY CROSSING THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE LOW ENDPOINT: the 16 h figure and the curve behind it are on a 2'-MOE GAPMER whose linkages are stated verbatim to be 'all ... phosphodiester', with a NAD-dependent ligase - NOT our fully modified 2'-OMe/2'-F phosphorothioate duplex, and the same patent's phosphorothioate/MOE figures are 11.8 percent or less. So the endpoint is transferred across backbone and enzyme class, not measured in our system. Which regime even applies - a batch hold or a packed-column residence - depends on the enzyme form, which is undecided (Q-050). The 5-20 min immobilised flow regime stays excluded, for a better reason than 'a different regime': a 5 mL column holding grams of immobilised enzyme is a fundamentally different enzyme-to-substrate ratio. See Q-010.

name: Ligase loading in the ligation reaction
scale_system: no single scale or system can be stated: the cited loadings are in mutually inconvertible units, and the one most often quoted (1 mg/mL cell-free extract) is 96-WELL PLATE SCREENING at 0.1 mM blockmer (SRC-ALMAC-2023 SI Table S1), not the 1 L run
notes: Value deliberately BLANK, on the P-HBEL-DS pattern: a registered gap, never invented. SCALE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 2026-09-25 - this row previously attributed 1 mg/mL of RNA ligase / PNK cell-free extract to '1 L scale'. SRC-ALMAC-2023's SI Table S1 is titled 'Reaction conditions for RNAL screening' and runs at 0.1 mM blockmer in 96-well plates; the paper reports NO loading for the 1 mM / 1 L run, so the guard on this row is vindicated and for a sharper reason than it carried. THE STRONGER REASON IS THAT A SINGLE LOADING CANNOT BE WRITTEN EVEN WITHIN ONE BRANCH, because the units do not convert: a Weiss unit is 'equivalent to approximately 200 cohesive end units (CEU)' on one vendor's own statement, a ~200x spread for the same enzyme, and neither assay uses our bond - SRC-PBCV1-2014 measures a ~100x drop in kcat for one enzyme between the all-DNA and RNA-splinted versions of the same sequence. Five mutually inconvertible loading units are in use across the estate, two of them inside one patent, and the bridge quantities that would reconcile them (specific activity in U/mg, a ligase mass beside a unit figure, an immobilisation yield) are absent everywhere. The loadings are therefore carried as PER-BRANCH rows in envelopes.csv, each in its own units and each with its own scale, which is what that register exists for. Also struck: SRC-CODEXIS-PATENTS' '0.01 g/L to about 50 g/L' must NOT be used to bracket this row - its subject is a single-stranded RNA ligase in a family with zero occurrences of 'splint', and in a sibling family the same range attaches to a purine nucleosidase. Stating any loading here would silently pick a form. See Q-050, Q-032, R-017.

name: Duplex melting temperature (Tm)
scale_system: bench UV thermal denaturation, 21-nt siRNA duplexes with THREE modified guide-strand positions in 100 mM NaCl - NOT a fully modified duplex and NOT our sequence (SRC-MALEK-2019)
notes: BAND: 58.1 C for the unmodified parent 21-mer, up to 64.1 C with 2'-F at three positions (SRC-MALEK-2019, Table 1). Point value deliberately BLANK: the authors report a +1 to +2 C/nt increment measured over THREE positions, and extrapolating it across all 21 positions of our fully modified duplex would invent a number. The band is what is measured; our sequence's Tm is unknown (Q-030). Tm sits ABOVE the moisture-shifted powder Tg of 38-53 C (P-DS-TG), so Tg binds first and Tm is the looser limit (Q-039). Also the reference for R-021: an 85 C enzyme denature hold sits well above this band. See R-003.

name: Glass transition of the dried product at its residual moisture
scale_system: bench; spray-dried trehalose siRNA POLYPLEX formulations, their matrix and their achieved moisture, not ours (SRC-KEIL-2021)
notes: BAND: measured Tg 38-53 C for spray-dried trehalose siRNA formulations at 3.8-4.6% residual moisture (SRC-KEIL-2021; NOT the 117 C anhydrous-trehalose figure an earlier draft carried). Point value deliberately BLANK: Tg is a function of OUR matrix and OUR achieved moisture (EQ-TG, Gordon-Taylor), neither of which is fixed - the excipient ratio is open (Q-021, P-EXCIPIENT-RATIO) and so is where it enters (Q-038). This is the BINDING thermal limit on drying and storage, tighter than Tm (P-DS-TM, Q-030). See Q-039, R-003.

name: Residual moisture in the dried product
scale_system: bench; spray-dried trehalose siRNA POLYPLEX formulations at their own dryer conditions, not ours (SRC-KEIL-2021)
notes: BAND: 3.8-4.6% w/w residual moisture measured on the trehalose formulations whose Tg was 38-53 C (SRC-KEIL-2021); their mannitol formulations dried far further, to 0.2-0.4%. Point value deliberately BLANK: residual moisture is an OUTCOME of our dryer outlet temperature and matrix (P-DRY-T-OUT, Q-046, Q-021), not an input we may assert. It is carried because it is the moisture at which that Tg band was measured - quoting the Tg without it would detach the number from its condition (EQ-TG). See Q-039.

name: Enzyme (ligase) clearance, log reduction
scale_system: no scale or system: no such measurement exists in the public record for either enzyme form
notes: Value deliberately BLANK, on the P-HBEL-DS pattern: a registered gap, never invented. No ppm, log-reduction, immunoassay or total-protein figure for ligase clearance exists in any patent, paper or vendor document the source dive read, and it read the whole relevant patent estate (Q-032). A full-text search of the strongest immobilised route for 'residual protein', 'ppm', 'ng/mg', 'ELISA', 'log reduction' and 'host cell' returns ZERO hits (SRC-CN119265174). This is the linchpin of the chromatography-free thesis (R-002), and it is blank for BOTH branches of Q-050, not just the immobilised one. See Q-032, Q-050, R-002, R-017, R-021.

name: Mass extinction coefficient at 260 nm (duplex)
scale_system: nucleic acid generally; SEQUENCE-SPECIFIC in reality and our sequence is not fixed
notes: BAND: 20-25 mL/mg/cm, bracketing the standard A260 = 1 conversions for nucleic acid (about 40-50 ug/mL at 1 cm) and allowing for duplex hypochromicity. Point value deliberately BLANK: the coefficient is sequence-specific, so a single number would assert a quantitation basis we do not have. Used ONLY to decide whether an in-line optical reading is geometrically possible on a stream (gen/controls.py), never to quantify anything. See Q-052, Q-042.

name: Minimum published pathlength, in-line variable-pathlength UV cell
scale_system: FlowVPE in-line process flow cell as published by the vendor; the published service is PROTEIN at A280, not an oligonucleotide at A260. FlowVPX does NOT publish a minimum at all
notes: 'pathlengths between 5 microns and 8 millimeters' (SRC-REPLIGEN-FLOWVPE). A vendor product specification, so it is a fact about the PRODUCT and nothing more. This is the floor the required pathlength is compared against to decide whether a reading can be taken in-line on a given stream; at P-CONC-UF the requirement falls below it, which is why C-013 is at_line_only. FlowVPX gives a maximum of 5.000 mm and a minimum STEP of 0.001 mm but never a minimum achievable pathlength, so this floor may not be the binding one for that instrument. See Q-051, Q-042.

name: Blockmer anneal temperature
scale_system: measured, bench - blockmers annealed at 2x final concentration in reaction buffer before every ligation; fully modified siRNA blockmers (PS + GalNAc) (SRC-ALMAC-2023). The CONDITION is explicit in the demonstrated route; the vessel it is performed in at 1 L is not stated
notes: Verbatim from the only demonstrated fully modified siRNA ligation route: blockmers are annealed in reaction buffer 'for 15 min at 65 C', then 'cooled to RT before being kept on ice until reactions were set up' (SRC-ALMAC-2023). Registered 2026-09-25 because the anneal was carried nowhere despite being non-optional - a double-stranded-RNA ligase needs a duplex nick, so every ligation is preceded by an anneal (Q-001). IT IS THE LARGEST THERMAL DUTY AT THIS STEP BY THREE ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE: the ramp to 65 C and back is a sensible-heat duty of order 170 kJ per kg of solution, against a reaction enthalpy of order 0.1 kJ per kg even taking a pyrophosphate-hydrolysis analogue as an upper bound, so the reaction enthalpy is negligible and the ramp is the whole duty (arithmetic ours; no calorimetric enthalpy for a ligation is published). NO UTILITY IN THE REGISTER HEATS A REACTOR JACKET - UT-STEAM is evaporator duty plus SIP and UT-CHILL is cooling - so this parameter has a duty and no utility behind it, which is Q-065 and UT-HOTW. Note this is a heating gap for the ANNEAL and bears on neither Q-050 nor the denature-unit question: U01-LIG already exists and is the right vessel. See P-LIG-ANNEAL-HOLD, Q-065.

name: Blockmer anneal hold time
scale_system: measured, bench - 96-well and bench anneal before ligation; fully modified siRNA blockmers (SRC-ALMAC-2023). NOT demonstrated at 1 L and NOT achievable at 1000 L in the same vessel, see notes
notes: Verbatim 'for 15 min at 65 C' (SRC-ALMAC-2023), paired with P-LIG-ANNEAL-T because a hold time quoted without its temperature is detached from its condition. THE NUMBER DOES NOT SURVIVE SCALE-UP AND THAT IS WHY IT IS REGISTERED: for geometrically similar vessels the heat-transfer area per unit volume falls as the cube root of the volume, so going from 1 L to 1000 L loses exactly 10x in specific area and a 15 min ramp becomes of order 150 min at the same jacket temperature difference - or the anneal leaves the reactor for a higher-area device (first principles, ours; no source states this for a ligation). That is an unregistered equipment fork and it sizes both the U01-LIG jacket and its temperature-control unit. See Q-065, UT-HOTW.

name: Enzyme thermal inactivation hold temperature
scale_system: bench batch ligations in two independent patents; low end 80 C on an IMMOBILISED crude RNA ligase at 50 uM substrate (SRC-CN119265174 Example 7), high end 95 C on soluble engineered ligases at 20-25 uM segment (SRC-USPTO-10640812 Examples 4, 5, 6, 8). Neither is our kg-scale batch and NEITHER IS A KILL VALIDATED AGAINST A RESIDUAL-PROTEIN MEASUREMENT
notes: BAND (evidence): the thermal inactivation conditions actually used in the documented ligation routes, 80-95 C, from two independent patents with different assignees, enzymes and enzyme forms - 80 C for 5 min (SRC-CN119265174 Example 7) and 95 C for 5 and for 10 min (SRC-USPTO-10640812), with 85 C for 15 min (SRC-CN119265174 Example 12) and 95 C for 20 min (SRC-WO2025262452) inside the band. POINT VALUE DELIBERATELY BLANK, and for a reason stronger than uncertainty: the step may not exist at all. In SRC-CN119265174 Examples 3, 5, 6 and 8 the immobilised enzyme is removed by centrifugation at 3000 rpm for 2 min with NO thermal hold, and Example 8 is immobilised AND batch AND unheated - so the hold is decided neither by soluble-versus-immobilised (the framing this register used, refuted) nor by batch-versus-flow (refuted by the same example). One document contradicts itself on this and the contradiction is published rather than resolved (Q-059). A 45 C LOW ENDPOINT CIRCULATED DURING RESEARCH AND IS REFUSED HERE: the document behind it could not be retrieved, and the figures offered for it are midpoints of residual-activity curves after a 60 min hold rather than melting temperatures. Nor may the inverse be written - 'neither 85 nor 95 C is needed' is NOT supported, because four independent documents chose 80-95 C. Almac's 75 C for 10-30 min is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY and is excluded from the band: it is the polynucleotide-kinase kill, applied to single strands before annealing, at 0.5 mM in 96-well plates (SRC-ALMAC-2023). EVERY VALUE IN THIS BAND SITS ABOVE THE DUPLEX MELTING BAND (P-DS-TM, 58.1-64.1 C), which is why R-021 is a live product risk rather than a theoretical one - and note the hazard is hydrolysis and depurination DURING the hold with Mg2+ still present, not melting, which is reversible. See R-021, R-022, C-014, Q-059, Q-050.

name: Blockmer / segment charge concentration at ligation
scale_system: no single scale or system: the two figures that bracket it are a 5 mL recirculated packed-bed run on a PHOSPHODIESTER 2'-MOE gapmer (SRC-USPTO-10640812) and an unquantified batch observation on fully modified siRNA blockmers at unstated scale (SRC-ALMAC-2023)
notes: Value deliberately BLANK and DELIBERATELY NO RANGE, which is the point of the row. The span 1.5-10 mM that the evidence appears to bracket FAILS the two-independent-endpoints test in a way no width can repair: its low end is a SUCCESS and its high end is a FAILURE, so the two ends are different KINDS of claim and the interval between them is not a range. Low: 1.5 mM of each segment reaching 89.50 percent product at 16 h (SRC-USPTO-10640812 Example 13, Table 22) - but on a substrate stated verbatim to have 'all linkages are phosphodiester linkages', with a NAD-dependent ligase, in 50 mM KH2PO4 with no Tris, no DTT and no ATP, so it crosses backbone, cofactor and buffer all at once. High: 10 mM blockmer, where reactions were verbatim 'slow and failed to go completion' (SRC-ALMAC-2023) - qualitative, with no conversion, time, temperature, enzyme or scale attached. Between 1.5 and 10 mM there is NO datapoint of any kind, a 6.7x void, and it is exactly where a plant would want to operate. Published as that shape rather than smoothed into a band. The related product-side figure, and the one the balance actually reads, is P-CONC-LIG. Registered in envelopes.csv with bracket_verdict not_a_range. See Q-064, Q-016, Q-066.
